item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q026_protein_kinase_like_function_transfer","answer":"SCOPe currently identifies base release 2.08 (stable label 2.08-stable; latest periodic-update label 2.08-2026-08-16). In this release, all three catalytic domains belong to the protein kinase-like fold d.144 and, more significantly, the protein kinase-like superfamily d.144.1 within the alpha-and-beta (a+b) class d. They occupy separate families: canonical protein-kinase catalytic subunits d.144.1.7 (SUNID 88854), aminoglycoside/APH phosphotransferases d.144.1.6 (SUNID 64411), and phosphoinositide 3-kinase catalytic domains d.144.1.4 (SUNID 56171). Because the relationship is at superfamily—not merely fold—level, SCOPe supports remote common ancestry and a conserved protein-kinase-like catalytic framework. Mechanistically, it supports a shared broad strategy of nucleotide-dependent phosphoryl transfer and related catalytic-domain architecture. It does not imply orthology, recent homology, identical substrates, or interchangeable regulation: canonical kinases principally phosphorylate protein residues, APHs phosphorylate aminoglycoside antibiotics, and PI3Ks phosphorylate the 3-hydroxyl of phosphoinositide lipids.
